originality.rationale: The central assertion is a necessary and sufficient zero-upper-/zero-lower-entropy criterion for all deterministic binary schedules, not the known transfer-matrix recipe or periodically forbidden-word capacity. The closest moving-hole generalizations require at least three symbols and explicitly identify the binary case as excluded. An already recorded higher-alphabet finite-prefix count excludes base two and supplies no such zero-rate characterization. The periodic subclass is acknowledged as covered by periodic-finite-type capacity theory. Full primary theorem statements and relevant proof contexts were inspected as detailed below; no equivalent coverage was located. Priority in specialized matrix-cocycle literature remains a stated risk.
residual_risks: A specialized nonautonomous matrix-product or constrained-code theorem not returned by topical/alias searches might entail the iff criterion.

The periodic alternating example is not offered as an independent new result; periodic-finite-type formulas likely cover it.

value.rationale: This is a sharp full classification of zero survivor growth for a canonical two-hole binary open map under every deterministic scheduling law, complementing recent b>=3 theories that expressly omit base two. It exposes a singular effect: both constant holes have entropy log(phi) but sparse-defect alternating switching has zero growth, maximum escape exponent log2, and a countable periodic-target survivor for perfect alternation. The exact finite-time bounds quantify this for all nonperiodic schedules; neither routine periodic capacity nor basic matrix-coding alone gives the all-schedule boundary.
